## Method 2

**This method predicts the exact score: Principal Component Regression estimates the numeric quality of each wine.**

## Phase I: Exploratory analysis

```{r phase1_1}
library(psych)
library(ggplot2)
library(GGally)
library(corrplot)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(gridExtra)
library(EnvStats)

# Download the UCI white wine data on the first run
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
wine_file <- "data/winequality-white.csv"
if (!file.exists(wine_file)) {
  download.file("https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/wine-quality/winequality-white.csv",
                destfile = wine_file)
}

wine <- read.csv(wine_file, sep = ";")

# Factor version of the score (for colouring plots)
wine$quality_factor <- as.factor(wine$quality)

# DISTRIBUTION OF THE SCORES

plot_scores <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = quality)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "lightpink", color = "black", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 3:9) +
  geom_text(stat = 'count', aes(label = after_stat(count)), vjust = -0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of the wine scores",
       x = "Score (quality)", y = "Number of wines")

plot_scores

# MEAN PROFILES

mean_table <- wine %>%
  group_by(quality) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)))

mean_table

```

```{r phase1_2}
# NORMALITY DIAGNOSTICS (same in both methods)

# Shapiro-Wilk test
shapiro_results <- lapply(wine[, 1:11], shapiro.test)
p_values <- sapply(shapiro_results, function(x) x$p.value)

print(p_values)

# Q-Q plots: alcohol, residual sugar, density, pH
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
qqnorm(wine$alcohol, main = "Q-Q plot: alcohol"); qqline(wine$alcohol, col = "#FF1493")
qqnorm(wine$residual.sugar, main = "Q-Q plot: residual sugar"); qqline(wine$residual.sugar, col = "#FF1493")
qqnorm(wine$density, main = "Q-Q plot: density"); qqline(wine$density, col = "#FF1493")
qqnorm(wine$pH, main = "Q-Q plot: pH"); qqline(wine$pH, col = "#FF1493")

# Q-Q plots: fixed acidity, volatile acidity, citric acid, chlorides
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
qqnorm(wine$fixed.acidity, main = "Q-Q plot: fixed acidity"); qqline(wine$fixed.acidity, col = "#FF1493")
qqnorm(wine$volatile.acidity, main = "Q-Q plot: volatile acidity"); qqline(wine$volatile.acidity, col = "#FF1493")
qqnorm(wine$citric.acid, main = "Q-Q plot: citric acid"); qqline(wine$citric.acid, col = "#FF1493")
qqnorm(wine$chlorides, main = "Q-Q plot: chlorides"); qqline(wine$chlorides, col = "#FF1493")

# Q-Q plots: free sulfur dioxide, sulphates, total sulfur dioxide
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
qqnorm(wine$free.sulfur.dioxide, main = "Q-Q plot: free sulfur dioxide"); qqline(wine$free.sulfur.dioxide, col = "#FF1493")
qqnorm(wine$sulphates, main = "Q-Q plot: sulphates"); qqline(wine$sulphates, col = "#FF1493")
qqnorm(wine$total.sulfur.dioxide, main = "Q-Q plot: total sulfur dioxide"); qqline(wine$total.sulfur.dioxide, col = "#FF1493")

# Filliben (probability plot correlation coefficient) test
filliben_results <- lapply(wine[, 1:11], function(x) gofTest(x, test = "ppcc", distribution = "norm"))

filliben_correlations <- sapply(filliben_results, function(x) x$statistic)
cat("\nQ-Q plot correlations\n")
print(filliben_correlations)


# SCATTER PLOT MATRICES (same in both methods)

# Panel 1: fixed acidity, volatile acidity, citric acid and pH
panel_acidity <- ggpairs(
  wine,
  columns = c("fixed.acidity", "volatile.acidity", "citric.acid", "pH"),
  mapping = aes(color = quality_factor),
  lower = list(continuous = wrap("points", alpha = 0.3, size = 0.5)),
  title = "Panel 1: scatter plot matrix, acidity profile"
) + theme_minimal()

print(panel_acidity)

# Panel 2: residual sugar, alcohol, density
panel_body <- ggpairs(
  wine,
  columns = c("residual.sugar", "alcohol", "density"),
  mapping = aes(color = quality_factor),
  lower = list(continuous = wrap("points", alpha = 0.3, size = 0.5)),
  title = "Panel 2: scatter plot matrix, body and sweetness"
) + theme_minimal()

print(panel_body)

# Panel 3: free and total sulfur dioxide, chlorides and sulphates
panel_preservatives <- ggpairs(
  wine,
  columns = c("free.sulfur.dioxide", "total.sulfur.dioxide", "chlorides", "sulphates"),
  mapping = aes(color = quality_factor),
  lower = list(continuous = wrap("points", alpha = 0.3, size = 0.5)),
  title = "Panel 3: scatter plot matrix, preservatives and minerals"
) + theme_minimal()

print(panel_preservatives)


# Correlation matrix: 11 chemical variables + quality
cor_matrix <- cor(wine[, c(1:11, 12)])

corrplot(cor_matrix, method = "number", type = "lower",
         tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45,
         number.cex = 0.7, col = colorRampPalette(c("#BB4444", "#FFFFFF", "#4477AA"))(200),
         title = "Correlation matrix",
         mar = c(0, 0, 1, 0))

```

## Phase II: Skewness and log transform

```{r phase2}
library(e1071)

# Skewness of the 11 chemical variables, from most to least skewed
skewness_values <- sapply(wine[, 1:11], skewness)
skewness_sorted <- sort(skewness_values, decreasing = TRUE)

print(skewness_sorted)

df_skewness <- data.frame(Variable = names(skewness_sorted),
                          Skewness = skewness_sorted)
df_skewness$Variable <- factor(df_skewness$Variable, levels = df_skewness$Variable)

skewness_plot <- ggplot(df_skewness, aes(x = Variable, y = Skewness, fill = Skewness > 1)) +
  geom_col(color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "pink", "FALSE" = "lightblue"),
                    name = "High skewness (> 1)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        aspect.ratio = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Skewness of each variable",
       x = "Variable",
       y = "Skewness coefficient")

print(skewness_plot)


# Effect of the transform (residual sugar as an example)

p_orig_hist <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = residual.sugar)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "lightblue", color = "black") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Residual sugar (original)", x = "g/dm³", y = "Frequency")

p_log_hist <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = log10(residual.sugar))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "pink", color = "black") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Residual sugar (log10)", x = "log10(g/dm³)", y = "Frequency")

grid.arrange(p_orig_hist, p_log_hist, ncol = 2)


# Stabilised dataset: log10 only on the variables with skewness > 1 (pink bars)
wine_pca <- wine %>%
  mutate(
    log_chlorides = log10(chlorides),
    log_volatile.acidity = log10(volatile.acidity),
    log_free.SO2 = log10(free.sulfur.dioxide),
    log_citric.acid = log10(citric.acid + 0.01), # +0.01 avoids log10(0)
    log_residual.sugar = log10(residual.sugar)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-chlorides, -volatile.acidity, -free.sulfur.dioxide, -citric.acid, -residual.sugar)

```

## Phase III: Dimensionality reduction (PCA)

```{r phase3}
library(FactoMineR)
library(factoextra)

# Numeric predictors only (any_of() drops the column if it exists and does not fail otherwise)
numeric_data <- wine_pca %>%
  dplyr::select(-quality, -dplyr::any_of("quality_factor"))

# Components and variance criterion
pca_result <- PCA(numeric_data, scale.unit = TRUE, ncp = 11, graph = FALSE)

eig_val <- get_eigenvalue(pca_result)
print(eig_val)

# Contribution (%) of each variable to PC1 and PC2
var_pca <- get_pca_var(pca_result)
print(round(var_pca$contrib[, 1:2], 2))

```

## Phase IV: Principal Component Regression (PCR) and evaluation

```{r phase4}
# First 6 components (6 PCs already retain 81.7% of the cumulative variance)
model_data <- as.data.frame(pca_result$ind$coord[, 1:6])
model_data$quality <- wine_pca$quality


# TRAIN (60%), VALIDATION (20%) AND TEST (20%) SPLIT

set.seed(123)
n_total <- nrow(model_data)
shuffled_idx <- sample(1:n_total)
train_cut <- round(0.60 * n_total)
val_cut   <- round(0.80 * n_total)

train_idx <- shuffled_idx[1:train_cut]
val_idx   <- shuffled_idx[(train_cut + 1):val_cut]
test_idx  <- shuffled_idx[(val_cut + 1):n_total]

train_data <- model_data[train_idx, ]
val_data   <- model_data[val_idx, ]
test_data  <- model_data[test_idx, ]

cat("Sizes - train:", nrow(train_data), "| validation:", nrow(val_data), "| test:", nrow(test_data), "\n\n")


# FIT THREE LINEAR REGRESSION MODELS (lm)

pcr_4pc <- lm(quality ~ Dim.1 + Dim.2 + Dim.3 + Dim.4, data = train_data)
pcr_5pc <- lm(quality ~ Dim.1 + Dim.2 + Dim.3 + Dim.4 + Dim.5, data = train_data)
pcr_6pc <- lm(quality ~ Dim.1 + Dim.2 + Dim.3 + Dim.4 + Dim.5 + Dim.6, data = train_data)


# MODEL SELECTION ON THE VALIDATION SET

pred_4pc <- predict(pcr_4pc, newdata = val_data)
pred_5pc <- predict(pcr_5pc, newdata = val_data)
pred_6pc <- predict(pcr_6pc, newdata = val_data)

# Mean absolute error: by how many points the model misses the real score
mae_4pc <- mean(abs(pred_4pc - val_data$quality))
mae_5pc <- mean(abs(pred_5pc - val_data$quality))
mae_6pc <- mean(abs(pred_6pc - val_data$quality))

cat("Validation mean absolute error\n")
cat("MAE (4 PCs):", round(mae_4pc, 3), "points\n")
cat("MAE (5 PCs):", round(mae_5pc, 3), "points\n")
cat("MAE (6 PCs):", round(mae_6pc, 3), "points\n")


# BLIND TEST WITH THE 6-PC MODEL

final_predictions <- predict(pcr_6pc, newdata = test_data)

final_mae <- mean(abs(final_predictions - test_data$quality))
cat("Final test MAE:", round(final_mae, 3), "points\n")

# "Pseudo confusion matrix": predictions are continuous, so round them first
rounded_predictions <- round(final_predictions)

hit_table <- table(Actual = test_data$quality, Predicted = rounded_predictions)
cat("Hit table (rounded predictions)\n")
print(hit_table)

# Exact accuracy and accuracy within a 1-point tolerance
exact_accuracy <- mean(rounded_predictions == test_data$quality) * 100
tolerant_accuracy <- mean(abs(rounded_predictions - test_data$quality) <= 1) * 100

cat("\nExact accuracy:", round(exact_accuracy, 2), "%\n")
cat("Tolerant accuracy (within +/- 1 point):", round(tolerant_accuracy, 2), "%\n")


# EXPERIMENT WITH 7 AND 11 COMPONENTS
# How low can the error go? (The small gain is not worth the extra components.)

all_pc_data <- as.data.frame(pca_result$ind$coord[, 1:11])
all_pc_data$quality <- wine_pca$quality

# Same train/validation split as above
set.seed(123)
n_total <- nrow(all_pc_data)
shuffled_idx <- sample(1:n_total)

train_cut <- round(0.60 * n_total)
val_cut   <- round(0.80 * n_total)

train_idx <- shuffled_idx[1:train_cut]
val_idx   <- shuffled_idx[(train_cut + 1):val_cut]

train_all <- all_pc_data[train_idx, ]
val_all   <- all_pc_data[val_idx, ]

pcr_7pc <- lm(quality ~ Dim.1 + Dim.2 + Dim.3 + Dim.4 + Dim.5 + Dim.6 + Dim.7, data = train_all)

# '.' means "use every available column" (all 11 PCs)
pcr_11pc <- lm(quality ~ ., data = train_all)

pred_7pc  <- predict(pcr_7pc, newdata = val_all)
pred_11pc <- predict(pcr_11pc, newdata = val_all)

mae_7pc  <- mean(abs(pred_7pc - val_all$quality))
mae_11pc <- mean(abs(pred_11pc - val_all$quality))

cat("MAE (7 PCs):", round(mae_7pc, 3), "points\n")
cat("MAE (11 PCs, the upper bound):", round(mae_11pc, 3), "points\n")
```

## Phase V: Outliers and robustness

```{r phase5}
# VISUAL INSPECTION OF OUTLIERS
# factor(quality) gives one box per score (3 to 9)

# Panel 1: acidity profile
p_fixed <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = factor(quality), y = fixed.acidity, fill = factor(quality))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + theme_minimal() + guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(title = "Fixed acidity", x = "", y = "g/dm³")

p_volatile <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = factor(quality), y = volatile.acidity, fill = factor(quality))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + theme_minimal() + guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(title = "Volatile acidity", x = "", y = "g/dm³")

p_citric <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = factor(quality), y = citric.acid, fill = factor(quality))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + theme_minimal() + guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(title = "Citric acid", x = "", y = "g/dm³")

p_pH <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = factor(quality), y = pH, fill = factor(quality))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + theme_minimal() + guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(title = "pH", x = "Score (quality)", y = "pH")

grid.arrange(p_fixed, p_volatile, p_citric, p_pH, ncol = 2,
             top = "Panel 1: acidity profile by score (distribution and outliers)")


# Panel 2: body and sweetness
p_sugar <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = factor(quality), y = residual.sugar, fill = factor(quality))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + theme_minimal() + guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(title = "Residual sugar", x = "", y = "g/dm³")

p_alcohol <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = factor(quality), y = alcohol, fill = factor(quality))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + theme_minimal() + guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(title = "Alcohol", x = "", y = "% vol.")

p_density <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = factor(quality), y = density, fill = factor(quality))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + theme_minimal() + guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(title = "Density", x = "Score (quality)", y = "g/cm³")

grid.arrange(p_sugar, p_alcohol, p_density, ncol = 2,
             top = "Panel 2: body and sweetness by score (distribution and outliers)")


# Panel 3: preservatives and minerals
p_free <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = factor(quality), y = free.sulfur.dioxide, fill = factor(quality))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + theme_minimal() + guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(title = "Free sulfur dioxide", x = "", y = "mg/dm³")

p_total <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = factor(quality), y = total.sulfur.dioxide, fill = factor(quality))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + theme_minimal() + guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(title = "Total sulfur dioxide", x = "", y = "mg/dm³")

p_chlor <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = factor(quality), y = chlorides, fill = factor(quality))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + theme_minimal() + guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(title = "Chlorides", x = "Score (quality)", y = "g/dm³")

p_sulph <- ggplot(wine, aes(x = factor(quality), y = sulphates, fill = factor(quality))) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + theme_minimal() + guides(fill = "none") +
  labs(title = "Sulphates", x = "Score (quality)", y = "g/dm³")

grid.arrange(p_free, p_total, p_chlor, p_sulph, ncol = 2,
             top = "Panel 3: preservatives and minerals by score (distribution and outliers)")


# OUTLIER DETECTION AND REMOVAL (1.5 x IQR RULE)

is_outlier <- function(x) {
  q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  lower <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
  upper <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr

  return(x < lower | x > upper)
}

# Numeric columns only, without the 'quality' score
numeric_vars <- wine_pca %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric), -quality)

outlier_counts <- sapply(numeric_vars, function(x) sum(is_outlier(x)))

cat("\n Outliers per variable (IQR rule) \n")
print(sort(outlier_counts, decreasing = TRUE))

# Cleaned dataset: keep only the rows that are not outliers in any column
wine_clean <- wine_pca
for (column in names(numeric_vars)) {
  wine_clean <- wine_clean[!is_outlier(wine_clean[[column]]), ]
}

cat("\n--- Effect of the cleaning ---\n")
cat("Original size:", nrow(wine_pca), "wines.\n")
cat("Cleaned size:", nrow(wine_clean), "wines.\n")
cat("Wines removed:", nrow(wine_pca) - nrow(wine_clean), "\n")

clean_chemistry <- wine_clean %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric), -quality)

pca_clean <- PCA(clean_chemistry, scale.unit = TRUE, ncp = 11, graph = FALSE)

clean_model_data <- as.data.frame(pca_clean$ind$coord[, 1:6])
clean_model_data$quality <- wine_clean$quality

# 80% train / 20% test
set.seed(123)
n_clean <- nrow(clean_model_data)
clean_idx <- sample(1:n_clean)

clean_train_cut <- round(0.80 * n_clean)
clean_train_idx <- clean_idx[1:clean_train_cut]
clean_test_idx  <- clean_idx[(clean_train_cut + 1):n_clean]

train_clean <- clean_model_data[clean_train_idx, ]
test_clean  <- clean_model_data[clean_test_idx, ]

cat("Cleaned sizes - train:", nrow(train_clean), "| test:", nrow(test_clean), "\n\n")


# EVALUATION

pcr_clean <- lm(quality ~ Dim.1 + Dim.2 + Dim.3 + Dim.4 + Dim.5 + Dim.6, data = train_clean)
pred_pcr_clean <- predict(pcr_clean, newdata = test_clean)

mae_clean <- mean(abs(pred_pcr_clean - test_clean$quality))
pred_pcr_rounded <- round(pred_pcr_clean)
tolerant_accuracy_clean <- mean(abs(pred_pcr_rounded - test_clean$quality) <= 1) * 100

cat("METHOD 2: REGRESSION (PCR)\n")
cat("MAE BEFORE: 0.599 | AFTER:", round(mae_clean, 3), "\n")
cat("Tolerant accuracy BEFORE: 93.98 % | AFTER:", round(tolerant_accuracy_clean, 2), "%\n")
```
